cra_reference: Art. 2-3; Annexes III-IV; Commission guidance C(2026) 5252
obligation_summary_paraphrase: Decide whether the product is a product with digital elements in scope, its class (default / important I / important II / critical) and exclusions
Record economic-operator role (manufacturer, authorised representative, importer, distributor) and EU establishment
verify_note: Verify article numbers for operator roles

obligation_summary_paraphrase: Assess cybersecurity risks and take the outcome into account in planning, design, development, production, delivery and maintenance
Document the risk assessment for intended purpose and reasonably foreseeable use; update it during the support period
evidence_type: Versioned risk register with change log
suggested_verification: Freshness check vs last product change (E4)

obligation_summary_paraphrase: Include risk assessment in technical documentation; justify any Annex I Part I requirement judged not applicable
Exercise due diligence when integrating third-party components, including free and open-source software
evidence_type: Component intake records, SBOM, supplier attestations

obligation_summary_paraphrase: Report vulnerabilities found in integrated components to their maintainers and share fixes where developed
Systematically document relevant cybersecurity aspects, including vulnerabilities and third-party information, and update the risk assessment
evidence_type: Security knowledge log linked to risk register

obligation_summary_paraphrase: Design, develop and produce the product to ensure an appropriate level of cybersecurity based on the risks
Made available without known exploitable vulnerabilities
evidence_type: Scan results + triage/VEX decisions for release build
verify_note: Release blocker independent of risk score

obligation_summary_paraphrase: Secure-by-default configuration, with possibility to reset to original state
Vulnerabilities can be addressed through security updates, incl. automatic updates by default with opt-out where applicable
verify_note: v1.0 placed secure updates under (h)-(m); correct letter is (c)

obligation_summary_paraphrase: Protection from unauthorised access by appropriate control mechanisms; report possible unauthorised access
verify_note: v1.0 labelled access/confidentiality/integrity as (c)-(g); correct letters (d)-(f)

obligation_summary_paraphrase: Protect confidentiality of stored, transmitted or processed data (e.g. state-of-the-art encryption)
Protect integrity of data, commands, programs and configuration; report corruption
Process only data adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary (data minimisation)
Protect availability of essential and basic functions, incl. resilience against denial-of-service
Minimise negative impact on availability of services provided by other devices or networks
Limit attack surfaces, including external interfaces
Reduce incident impact using exploitation mitigation mechanisms and techniques
Provide security-related information by recording/monitoring internal activity, with user opt-out
Users can securely and easily remove all data and settings permanently, and transfer data where possible
Identify and document vulnerabilities and components, incl. an SBOM covering at least top-level dependencies in a common machine-readable format
Address and remediate vulnerabilities without delay, incl. security updates; separate security from functionality updates where technically feasible
Apply effective and regular tests and reviews of product security
Once an update is available, share and publicly disclose information about fixed vulnerabilities (delay possible where justified)
Put in place and enforce a coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy
Facilitate sharing of information about potential vulnerabilities, incl. a contact address
Provide mechanisms to securely distribute updates, automatically where applicable
Disseminate security updates without delay and free of charge (unless otherwise agreed for tailor-made products), with advisory messages
Determine support period reflecting expected use; at least five years unless expected use is shorter; record the basis in technical documentation
Keep each security update available for at least 10 years after issue or for the remainder of the support period, whichever is longer
verify_note: Missing in v1.0; verify paragraph number on EUR-Lex

obligation_summary_paraphrase: Designate a single point of contact for vulnerability reporting that is easy to find (not only automated tools)
Product bears type/batch/serial number or other identification; manufacturer name, address and digital contact on product/packaging/docs
Provide Annex II user information and instructions, kept available for the required period
Notify actively exploited vulnerabilities via the Single Reporting Platform: early warning 24 h, notification 72 h, final report 14 days after corrective measure
Notify severe incidents having an impact on product security: early warning 24 h, notification 72 h, final report within one month of notification
Inform impacted users (and where appropriate all users) of the vulnerability/incident and mitigation measures
Voluntary reporting of other vulnerabilities, cyber threats, near misses
Draw up technical documentation before placing on the market and keep it updated
Keep technical documentation and EU DoC at disposal of authorities for at least 10 years or the support period, whichever is longer
verify_note: Missing in v1.0; verify paragraph number

obligation_summary_paraphrase: Carry out the applicable conformity assessment procedure (Module A / B+C / H / EUCC as required by class)
Draw up EU declaration of conformity and affix CE marking
Procedures to keep series production in conformity, considering changes in design, standards or specifications
Assess whether a change is a substantial modification re-triggering obligations
Open-source software steward obligations (only if acting as steward)
